# Challenge 1: Bounding Box {.subtitle}

## A bounding box is four numbers

- The **axis-aligned bounding box** of a set of points is the smallest rectangle (with sides parallel to the axes) that contains all of them
- Numerically: just four values

$$\text{BB} = (x_{\min},\ y_{\min},\ x_{\max},\ y_{\max})$$

- **Key insight:** you never need to store the full point list — only the current extremes

## The algorithm

Initialize with the first point:

$$x_{\min} = x_{\max} = x_0 \quad y_{\min} = y_{\max} = y_0$$

For every subsequent point $(x, y)$:

- if $x < x_{\min}$ → update $x_{\min}$
- if $x > x_{\max}$ → update $x_{\max}$
- if $y < y_{\min}$ → update $y_{\min}$
- if $y > y_{\max}$ → update $y_{\max}$

Four comparisons per point. Memory: constant (four numbers, regardless of stream length).

## R implementation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
stream <- matrix(c(
  2489750, 1117500,
  2506250, 1172500,
  2552750, 1223500,
  2498000, 1198000,
  2470000, 1145000
), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)

bb <- c(xmin = stream[1,1], xmax = stream[1,1],
        ymin = stream[1,2], ymax = stream[1,2])

for (i in seq_len(nrow(stream))) {
  bb["xmin"] <- min(bb["xmin"], stream[i, 1])
  bb["xmax"] <- max(bb["xmax"], stream[i, 1])
  bb["ymin"] <- min(bb["ymin"], stream[i, 2])
  bb["ymax"] <- max(bb["ymax"], stream[i, 2])
}
bb
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   xmin    xmax    ymin    ymax 
2470000 2552750 1117500 1223500 
```


:::
:::


# Challenge 2: Point in Polygon {.subtitle}

## The intuition

Draw a ray from the point horizontally to the right (→ infinity):

- Count how many **polygon edges** the ray crosses
- **Odd** number of crossings → point is **inside**
- **Even** number of crossings → point is **outside**


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](vector-data-solution_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=480}
:::
:::


## Ray casting: the algorithm

For each **edge** of the polygon (vertex $i$ → vertex $i+1$):

1. Does the edge **straddle** the horizontal line $y = p_y$?
   $$( y_i > p_y ) \ne ( y_{i+1} > p_y )$$

2. If yes: is the ray–edge intersection **to the right** of $p_x$?
   $$x_{\text{hit}} = x_i + \frac{(p_y - y_i)(x_{i+1} - x_i)}{y_{i+1} - y_i} > p_x$$

3. If both conditions hold → **flip** an `inside` boolean (starts `FALSE`)

Result: `inside` after all edges = TRUE if the point is inside.

## R implementation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
point_in_poly <- function(px, py, vx, vy) {
  n <- length(vx)
  inside <- FALSE
  j <- n
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (((vy[i] > py) != (vy[j] > py)) &&
        (px < (vx[j] - vx[i]) * (py - vy[i]) / (vy[j] - vy[i]) + vx[i])) {
      inside <- !inside
    }
    j <- i
  }
  inside
}

# polygon: a rough triangle
vx <- c(1, 4, 2.5); vy <- c(1, 1, 4)

point_in_poly(2.5, 2,   vx, vy)  # inside  → TRUE
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] TRUE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
point_in_poly(0,   0,   vx, vy)  # outside → FALSE
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] FALSE
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
point_in_poly(3.5, 3.5, vx, vy)  # outside → FALSE
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] FALSE
```


:::
:::


## Edge cases

| Situation | How to handle |
|---|---|
| Ray passes exactly through a vertex | Use strict `>` on one side, `>=` on the other — ensures each vertex is counted at most once |
| Point lies exactly on an edge | Technically undefined; most implementations return TRUE |
| Polygon is not closed | Close it: ensure last vertex = first vertex |
| Concave / complex polygons | Algorithm works unchanged — this is its strength over simpler methods |

  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
